cohort: The study included 253,901 females in Ontario, Canada, who had their first childbirth between 2012 and 2017 and had no pre-existing autoimmune disease.
finding: The study found a possible link between primary Cesarean delivery and the development of multiple sclerosis in women, but no association with celiac disease, rheumatoid arthritis, or systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with an increased risk of multiple sclerosis, with the largest effect observed between birth and 3 years postpartum, when compared to vaginal delivery.
